{"action":"write_file","content":"# Specification Quality Checklist: Batch Transactions (BatchWriter) for tinydb

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-10-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

## Content Quality

- [x] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
- [x] Focused on user value and business needs
- [x] Written for non-technical stakeholders
- [x] All mandatory sections completed

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain
- [x] Requirements are testable and unambiguous
- [x] Success criteria are measurable
- [x] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no implementation details)
- [x] All acceptance scenarios are defined
- [x] Edge cases are identified
- [x] Scope is clearly bounded
- [x] Dependencies and assumptions identified

## Feature Readiness

- [x] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria
- [x] User scenarios cover primary flows
- [x] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
- [x] No implementation details leak into specification

## Notes

- Items marked incomplete require spec updates before `$speckit-clarify` or
  `$speckit-plan`
- Validation performed 2026-10-19 by reviewing spec.md against each item:
  - Content Quality: spec describes the batch writer in terms of capabilities
    and observable behavior (apply a batch, rollback, results, data
    independence); no code, language, or framework details beyond the
    requirement-derived vocabulary ("default table", "mapping") mandated by
    the frozen R01-R03 requirement text.
  - Requirement Completeness: FR-001..FR-009 each map to an acceptance
    scenario in User Stories 1-3 or an Edge Case; no [NEEDS CLARIFICATION]
    markers; success criteria SC-001..SC-005 are 100%/count-based and
    verifiable without implementation knowledge.
  - Feature Readiness: primary flows (apply, fail/rollback, independence)
    covered by P1-P3 stories; edge cases cover malformed ops, missing IDs,
    in-batch insert-then-remove, non-list batches, and nested data.
- Scope boundary: default table only; multi-table batches, updates, and
  batch persistence are explicitly out of scope (see Assumptions).
- No open items; spec is ready for `$speckit-plan`.
", "path":"specs/001-transactions/checklists/requirements.md"}
